target.title: fix(agents): route provider-local-service health probe through fetchWithSsrFGuard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `probeHealth` function in `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:260` polls the operator-configured `service.healthUrl` via the un-guarded global `fetch`. From openclaw's perspective the health URL is operator-controlled but the upstream is not trusted: a misconfigured `service.healthUrl` (one whose DNS A record rebinds to a private/internal IP, or whose endpoint streams an unbounded body that the probe can't bound) currently bypasses every protection owned by `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. `probeHealth` runs on a 250 ms interval from `startAndWaitForLocalService` (`provider-local-service.ts:301`) until the local service becomes healthy, so an SSRF miss here is amplified into a repeated fetch loop against the hostile target.

This PR wraps the probe fetch with `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in STRICT mode and feeds it a narrow local-service SSRF policy (`resolveLocalServiceProbePolicy`) that supports loopback literal URLs (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`) without making public hostnames bypass the private-network block. The existing `.catch(...).finally(...)` chain (timeout translation, `controller.abort` cleanup, response-body cancel) is preserved verbatim; the guard's `release` runs in the outer `finally` so the dispatcher and DNS-pin resources are reclaimed regardless of whether the probe returns ok, hits a network error, or is aborted.

## Changes

- `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:5,13-14` — add `import { isLoopbackIpAddress } from "@openclaw/net-policy/ip"` and `import type { SsrFPolicy } from "../infra/net/ssrf.js"`.
- `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:222-263` — add `resolveLocalServiceProbePolicy(url)` helper. For loopback literal hostnames (`127.0.0.1`, `::1` unwrapped, `localhost`) it returns `{ allowedHostnames: [literal], hostnameAllowlist: [literal] }` so the guard skips private-network checks for the literal loopback. For any other hostname it returns `{ hostnameAllowlist: [hostname] }` only — the hostname check passes, but the guard still validates resolved IPs against the private-network block, so a public-looking healthUrl that DNS-resolves to a private IP is rejected. This addresses the round-1 ClawSweeper finding that target-derived `allowedHostnames` made every configured hostname bypass the private-network block (`ssrf.ts:229` `shouldSkipPrivateNetworkChecks`).
- `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:274-279` — `probeHealth` now calls `policy: resolveLocalServiceProbePolicy(url)` instead of the prior target-derived `policy: { allowedHostnames: [new URL(url).hostname] }`. The existing `clearTimeout`, `removeEventListener("abort", onAbort)`, and `await response?.body?.cancel?.()` cleanup runs unchanged.
- `src/agents/provider-local-service.test.ts` — 5 new policy unit tests (loopback IPv4, loopback IPv6, `localhost`, public hostname, look-local-but-isn't hostname) and 1 new end-to-end negative control (`blocks health probe when public-looking healthUrl resolves to a private IP via DNS rebind`) that injects a `lookupFn` returning `192.168.1.1` for a public-looking URL and asserts the guard rejects with `resolves to private`. The existing 12 tests drive `ensureModelProviderLocalService` end-to-end against real loopback and continue to pass unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `probeHealth` now routes its GET to `service.healthUrl` through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with a narrow local-service policy; DNS rebinding protection and the private-network block now apply to public-looking healthUrl hostnames while explicit loopback probe URLs still resolve and reach the local service.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-local-service.test.ts --run`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-local-service.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  18 passed (18)
    Start at  23:46:01
    Duration  4.36s
  ```
  - 12 pre-existing tests pass unchanged (real loopback probes via `freePort()` + `process.execPath` + inline `http.createServer` flow through the guard and succeed).
  - 5 new policy unit tests pass:
    - IPv4 loopback literal `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/models` → `{ allowedHostnames: ["127.0.0.1"], hostnameAllowlist: ["127.0.0.1"] }` (loopback literal accepted, private check skipped for the literal).
    - IPv6 loopback literal `http://[::1]:11434/v1/models` → `{ allowedHostnames: ["::1"], hostnameAllowlist: ["::1"] }` (URL brackets stripped before loopback check + allowlist).
    - `http://localhost:11434/v1/models` → `{ allowedHostnames: ["localhost"], hostnameAllowlist: ["localhost"] }` (operator-friendly alias works).
    - `http://api.example.com/v1/models` → `{ hostnameAllowlist: ["api.example.com"] }` only — `allowedHostnames` is **absent** (private-network block preserved against DNS rebind).
    - `http://my-service.internal/v1/models` → `hostnameAllowlist: ["my-service.internal"]` only — the `.internal` suffix does not bypass private checks.
  - 1 new end-to-end negative control test (`blocks health probe when public-looking healthUrl resolves to a private IP via DNS rebind`) passes: it calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` directly with `resolveLocalServiceProbePolicy("http://api.example.com/v1/models")` and a `lookupFn` returning `192.168.1.1`. The guard rejects with `Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address` and `fetchImpl` is never invoked. Reverting the helper back to the target-derived `allowedHostnames: [new URL(url).hostname]` shape makes this test fail (the private-network block is skipped for `api.example.com`).
- **Observed result after fix**: Real loopback probes continue to flow end-to-end through the guard, and a real public-looking URL with a hostile DNS-rebind answer is rejected before any network I/O. The narrow policy shape is the inverse of the round-1 finding: the only hostnames that get `allowedHostnames` (which triggers the private-network-check skip) are the loopback literals `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, and `localhost`.
- **What was not tested**: Live probe against a real managed local service deployment; the proof is unit-level via the production wrapper + loopback for the happy path and via the guard's own DNS-rebind path for the negative control, the same shape approved for prior fetch-guard wiring PRs.

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)

- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:299` (`streamProxy`) — sibling surface with the same pattern, submitted as a separate PR to keep each change XS.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts` and `src/infra/push-apns.relay.ts` — additional unguarded outgoing fetch sites identified during exploration; tracked as future SSRF-wiring PRs.

## Risk

- **Scope**: 1 prod file + 1 test file; +45 source LoC (net) + 61 test LoC.
- **Behavior**: Same outgoing request shape as before, plus a narrow policy object routed through `resolveLocalServiceProbePolicy`. `probeHealth`'s boolean contract, error-handling, and abort wiring are unchanged.
- **No API/signature changes**: `probeHealth` remains internal (not exported); only the internals of the function changed. `resolveLocalServiceProbePolicy` is a new export added to this module specifically so the test can verify the policy shape directly.
- **Compatibility**: All 12 pre-existing tests pass unchanged. The probe response-body `cancel()` in the outer `finally` still runs after `releaseGuarded()` so backpressure cleanup is preserved.
- **Type check**: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` clean on the touched branch.
- **Lint**: `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=4` clean (all three shards).
- **Sibling coordination**: Distinct file from `proxy.ts`; submitted as a separate PR. The new helper reuses the canonical `isLoopbackIpAddress` from `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` (same package `configured-local-origin-bypass.ts:3` imports for the analogous check).
